"""What an LLM caller is told when a move ends: reached and stopped short differ."""

import json
from pathlib import Path

from hebbian_rua.client.contract.station_api import (
    CommandCompletion,
    CommandOutcome,
    CommandRecord,
    TargetStatus,
)
from hebbian_rua.client.llm.robot_tools import records_result
from hebbian_rua.client.llm.types import RobotToolCall


def record(outcome: CommandOutcome, target_status: TargetStatus) -> CommandRecord:
    return CommandRecord(
        command_id="c",
        label="move_to_joints",
        accepted_at=0.0,
        checkpoints=[],
        completion=CommandCompletion(finished_at=1.0, outcome=outcome),
        target_status=target_status,
    )


def test_group_outcomes_match_the_shared_examples() -> None:
    examples = json.loads(
        (Path(__file__).parent / "fixtures/model-command-outcomes.json").read_text()
    )
    for example in examples:
        result = records_result(
            RobotToolCall(example["name"], "move_arms", {}),
            [CommandRecord.model_validate(example["record"])],
            grouped=True,
        )
        assert result.is_error is example["expected_error"]
        assert json.loads(result.text)["status"] == example["expected_status"]
        single = records_result(
            RobotToolCall(example["name"], "set_arm_gripper", {}),
            [CommandRecord.model_validate(example["record"])],
        )
        assert single.is_error is example["expected_error"]
        assert (
            json.loads(single.text)["completion"]["outcome"]
            == example["record"]["completion"]["outcome"]
        )


def test_an_interrupted_move_requires_recovery_not_a_hard_fault_stop() -> None:
    result = records_result(
        RobotToolCall("1", "move_to_joints", {}),
        [record(CommandOutcome.interrupted, TargetStatus.partial)],
    )
    assert result.is_error
    assert result.interrupted
    assert not result.halt
    assert '"outcome":"interrupted"' in result.text

# Inspect Blocks

Arrange some blocks, then ask a yes/no question such as "Are there more than two
blocks?" or "Are the blocks stacked?". The model drives the arm to inspect the
scene with the wrist camera and decides. The arm then nods for yes or shakes its
head for no.

The model chooses where to look with the robot tools. The gestures are fixed joint
moves, so the answer is always shown the same way.

## You need

- One SO-101 with [per-arm setup](https://github.com/Hebbian-Robotics/rua/blob/main/docs/hardware.md) done, resting on its
  table. The arm rehomes and disables between questions, and disabling drops it,
  so the start pose must be supported.
- A camera named `table` that the model can point, such as a wrist camera
  ([cameras](https://github.com/Hebbian-Robotics/rua/blob/main/docs/cameras.md)).
- A clear workspace, by default a mat in front of the arm. Questions only cover
  objects on it.
- `OPENAI_API_KEY` in your environment or `.env`.

## Run

Start the station with your profile and camera, then the app:

```sh
uv run rua serve --profile ~/.config/rua/so101.toml --camera table=0
uv run --project examples/python examples/applications/inspect-blocks/inspect_blocks.py --model <openai-model>
```

Type a question and press Enter; a blank line quits. Pass
`--workspace "the white tray left of the arm"` to describe a different area.

Each question writes the camera frames the model saw and the moves it made to
`runs/<time>/` next to the script. Open them to see why it answered as it did.

## Before the first run

- **Cap speed in the station.** The prompt asks for at most 0.6 rad/s, but a model
  can ignore that. Set `[motion] max_joint_speed` in your private profile so the
  station enforces a limit; we used 1.0 rad/s.
- **Check the presenting pose.** `PRESENT_JOINTS` was chosen on one arm to leave
  room for the nod before the wrist limit. Preview it on yours with
  `preview_pose`, or run the gestures alone, before asking questions.
- Keep a physical power cutoff within reach.

## What made the answers reliable

- **Name the workspace.** Without it, the model counted objects elsewhere on the
  desk. The prompt now limits every question to the workspace.
- **Look from the side.** From above, a stack looks like one block. The prompt asks
  for a low, side-on view before counting or judging stacking.
- **Ask for evidence.** The model states how many blocks it saw, where, and which
  are stacked before its `ANSWER:` line, so a wrong answer is easy to spot.
- **Log the frames.** The saved frames showed both failures above.

# Install from source

The published `hebbian-rua` wheel includes the SDK, native binaries and robot
models. Source development additionally needs Rust, Python and uv. This workflow
is exercised on Ubuntu 24.04 x86-64 and macOS 14+ (Apple Silicon).
Native Windows is not validated for RUA.
For Windows setup considerations, see [Windows with WSL2](windows-wsl.md).

Install [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), the pinned Rust toolchain and, on Ubuntu,
`build-essential`, `pkg-config`, `libudev-dev` and `mold`. On macOS, install
Xcode Command Line Tools (`xcode-select --install`) and use the default Apple
Clang compiler. From the checkout root:

```sh
uv run rua-dev setup
cargo build -p hebbian-station
uv sync --project examples/python --locked
```

Setup prepares the checksum-pinned SO-101 models in ignored `robots/so101` and
caches their release archive under `.cache/so101`. Once prepared, model assets
need no network access for builds or runs. Installed wheels need no setup step.

Run the station with your calibrated profile or simulator connected:

```sh
uv run rua serve --profile ./robot.toml
```

See [hardware setup](hardware.md), [simulator integration](simulators.md) and
[cameras](cameras.md) for the RUA connection steps. `uv run rua-dev --help` lists
checks and commands for the components included in your checkout.

## Optional viewer

If your checkout includes the TypeScript viewer, install Node.js and pnpm, then:

```sh
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm build
```

The station serves the resulting viewer assets from disk. Camera builds have
additional [native prerequisites](cameras.md#rua-configuration); recording needs
[FFmpeg](recording.md). Building the Rust server alone needs neither frontend
nor media build tools.

# Choose what the model sees

`RobotTools` keeps full station responses and formats a concise view for the
model. The same view works with the OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini adapters.

By default, observations show each arm once, with measured joints, tool pose,
gripper state, faults and interlocks. Motion results keep outcomes, achieved
poses and limits while omitting checkpoints, trace metadata and rendering
geometry. Sequence results show their phase, requested/recorded step counts and
the last step instead of repeating the whole history. Model views use rounded
millimetres and degrees; tool inputs still use metres and radians. Joint
velocities and efforts are retained in full output for diagnostics, rather than
included in the concise state. Full output preserves velocities in radians per
second and efforts in the hardware profile's units; efforts are not necessarily
torque in newton-metres.

## Full output

Pass a different view of your existing tools to any provider adapter:

```python
from hebbian_rua import full_formatter
from hebbian_rua.openai import OpenAIRobotTools

model_tools = OpenAIRobotTools(robot.map_output(full_formatter))
```

`robot` is your existing `RobotTools` instance. `full_formatter` shows all fields
in their original units and precision. It includes configured observation
cameras, notes and camera availability/timing information.

## Your own formatter

One function handles both observations and tool results. It receives full data,
not the default summary. Branch on `output.kind` or `output.call.name` when you
want different presentation for a particular tool.

```python
from hebbian_rua import ModelContent, RobotOutput, default_formatter
from hebbian_rua.openai import OpenAIRobotTools


def format_for_task(output: RobotOutput) -> ModelContent:
    content = default_formatter(output)
    if output.kind == "observation":
        # Keep the default state text, but send only the camera this task needs.
        cameras = {
            name: jpeg for name, jpeg in content.cameras.items() if name == "table"
        }
        return ModelContent(content.text, cameras)
    return content


model_tools = OpenAIRobotTools(robot.map_output(format_for_task))
```

`ModelContent` carries text and, for observations, camera JPEGs. Tool results
currently support text only; returning camera images for a result raises an
error. Observation inputs also include the selected arm, notes, unavailable
optional cameras and camera retrieval intervals. Preserve information your task
needs to interpret failures or stale views. Formatters should be pure functions;
callback exceptions propagate to the caller without retrying robot commands.

`map_output` returns a new view sharing the station and lease. It leaves the
original tools unchanged and replaces any previous formatter. Compose ordinary
functions inside your formatter when needed. Camera filtering changes model
content; it does not change configured required-camera checks or capture.
Formatting cannot change command execution or error, halt and interruption flags.
Close the shared station only after all views have finished using it.

## Application data and logging

With the lower-level SDK, `await robot.execute_one(call)` returns a
`RobotToolResult`; provider adapters also expose these as `turn.results`:

- `result.data`: complete station payload in original units and precision,
  or the original error text.
- `result.text`: the selected model-facing text.
- `result.model_data`: the selected text parsed as JSON when possible.

`await robot.observe()` returns `RobotObservation`, whose `data` is the full
station state, with selected model text and images in `text` and `cameras`.
Use `capture()` when you also need the original camera capture metadata.

Previously, `result.data` parsed the formatted text. Use `result.model_data` for
that behavior; use `result.data` for complete application data. The station
client itself and the CLI continue returning their existing full responses.

# Control model

The station manages robot state and accepts commands through its API. A client
acquires a control lease before sending motion commands. Other clients can
continue reading state and camera snapshots.

In Python, use `station.holding_lease(...)` and send motion through the returned
lease. Power, stop and state access are available through `station.arm(...)`.
Commands return outcomes; check them before proceeding to another action.

The station enforces configured joint limits and protective stops. These checks
require per-arm calibration and do not establish physical workspace clearance.
See [hardware setup](hardware.md) before operating a physical arm, and the
[Python example](../examples/python/hello_robot.py) for a small control program.

name: Publish

on:
  release:
    types: [published]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  UV_EXCLUDE_NEWER: "3 days"

concurrency:
  group: publish-${{ github.event.release.tag_name || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    if: github.repository == 'Hebbian-Robotics/rua'
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-24.04, macos-15]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803 # v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@c771a70e6277c0a99b617c7a806ffedaca235ff9 # v9.0.0
        with:
          version: "0.13.6"
          python-version: "3.14"
          enable-cache: true
      - name: Verify the release tag matches the package version
        env:
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ github.event.release.tag_name }}
        run: |
          package_version="$(uv version --short)"
          if [ "${GITHUB_EVENT_NAME}" = release ] && [ "${RELEASE_TAG}" != "v${package_version}" ]; then
            echo "Release tag ${RELEASE_TAG} must equal v${package_version}." >&2
            exit 1
          fi
      - name: Install Linux build tools
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://apt.llvm.org/llvm-snapshot.gpg.key | sudo gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/llvm.gpg
          echo 'deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/llvm.gpg] https://apt.llvm.org/noble/ llvm-toolchain-noble-21 main' | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/llvm.list
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y pkg-config mold libudev-dev libglib2.0-dev clang-21 libclang-21-dev ffmpeg
          {
            echo 'CC=clang-21'
            echo 'CXX=clang++-21'
          } >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - name: Install macOS build tools
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: |
          brew install ffmpeg pkg-config
          {
            echo 'CC=clang'
            echo 'CXX=clang++'
            echo 'MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=14.0'
            echo 'TMPDIR=/tmp'
          } >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - name: Restore Rust build cache
        uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@d1527c8f67ef9af357290475d4af4b0fab8f12e0 # v2.9.3
        with:
          shared-key: release-${{ matrix.os }}
          env-vars: CC CXX MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET
          save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' || github.event_name == 'release' }}
      - name: Check source and generated contracts
        run: |
          uv run --locked rua-dev setup
          uv run --locked rua-dev validate --lane python
          uv run --locked rua-dev contracts --check
      - name: Build the release wheel
        run: uv run --locked rua-dev package rua
      - name: Repair Linux libraries
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          uvx --with patchelf auditwheel repair --plat manylinux_2_39_x86_64 --wheel-dir dist/repaired dist/hebbian_rua-*.whl
      - name: Bundle macOS libraries
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: |
          uvx --from delocate delocate-wheel --require-archs "$(uname -m)" --wheel-dir dist/repaired dist/hebbian_rua-*.whl
      - name: Upload wheels for installation checks
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: rua-wheels-${{ matrix.os }}
          path: dist/repaired/*.whl
          if-no-files-found: error

  installed-wheel:
    needs: build
    strategy:
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-24.04, macos-15]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803 # v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@c771a70e6277c0a99b617c7a806ffedaca235ff9 # v9.0.0
        with:
          version: "0.13.6"
          python-version: "3.14"
          enable-cache: true
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: rua-wheels-${{ matrix.os }}
          path: dist/repaired
      - name: Verify a clean wheel installation and simulator connection
        run: |
          for wheel_path in dist/repaired/*.whl; do
            uv run --locked rua-dev package check "${wheel_path}"
          done

  publish:
    if: github.repository == 'Hebbian-Robotics/rua' && github.event_name == 'release'
    needs: installed-wheel
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    environment:
      name: pypi
      url: https://pypi.org/p/hebbian-rua
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          pattern: rua-wheels-*
          merge-multiple: true
          path: dist
      - name: Publish to PyPI
        uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@7245906fb61fa33a13554f9d5fb856fe61758086 # v1.14.3
        with:
          password: ${{ secrets.PYPI_API_TOKEN }}
      - name: Attach release wheels and checksums
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ github.event.release.tag_name }}
        run: |
          cd dist
          sha256sum ./*.whl > SHA256SUMS
          gh release upload "${RELEASE_TAG}" ./*.whl SHA256SUMS --clobber
    permissions:
      contents: write

name: Check

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  python:
    if: github.repository == 'Hebbian-Robotics/rua'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803 # v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@c771a70e6277c0a99b617c7a806ffedaca235ff9 # v9.0.0
        with:
          version: "0.13.6"
          python-version: "3.14"
          enable-cache: true
      - run: uv sync --locked
      - run: uv run rua-dev validate --lane python
      - run: uv lock --check --project examples/python

  rust:
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-24.04, macos-15]
    if: github.repository == 'Hebbian-Robotics/rua'
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803 # v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Install Linux build tools
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://apt.llvm.org/llvm-snapshot.gpg.key | sudo gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/llvm.gpg
          echo 'deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/llvm.gpg] https://apt.llvm.org/noble/ llvm-toolchain-noble-21 main' | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/llvm.list
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y pkg-config mold libudev-dev libglib2.0-dev clang-21 libclang-21-dev ffmpeg
          {
            echo 'CC=clang-21'
            echo 'CXX=clang++-21'
          } >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - name: Install macOS build tools
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: |
          brew install ffmpeg pkg-config
          {
            echo 'CC=clang'
            echo 'CXX=clang++'
            echo 'MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=14.0'
            echo 'TMPDIR=/tmp'
          } >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@c771a70e6277c0a99b617c7a806ffedaca235ff9 # v9.0.0
        with:
          version: "0.13.6"
          python-version: "3.14"
          enable-cache: true
      - name: Restore Rust build cache
        uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@d1527c8f67ef9af357290475d4af4b0fab8f12e0 # v2.9.3
        with:
          shared-key: checks-${{ matrix.os }}
          env-vars: CC CXX MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET
          save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' || github.event_name == 'release' }}
      - name: Prepare pinned robot assets
        run: uv run rua-dev setup
      - run: rustup show active-toolchain
      - run: cargo fmt --all -- --check
      - run: cargo clippy --locked --all-targets --all-features
      - run: cargo test --locked --workspace --all-features
      - run: uv run rua-dev contracts --check

[workspace]
resolver = "3"
members = ["robot-geometry", "contracts", "executor", "station", "station-access", "recordings", "livekit-cameras"]
default-members = ["robot-geometry", "contracts", "executor", "station", "station-access", "recordings"]
# livekit-cameras links libwebrtc (needs clang 21); build it with `-p livekit-cameras`.

[workspace.lints.clippy]
pedantic = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }
needless_pass_by_value = "allow"
unnecessary_wraps = "allow"
missing_panics_doc = "allow"

# Line tables alone keep stack traces and panic locations and cut target/ size.
[profile.dev]
debug = "line-tables-only"

# Video conversion needs optimization even when the rest of the station is built
# for development; otherwise live camera frames accumulate noticeable delay.
[profile.dev.package.cameras]
opt-level = 3

[profile.dev.package.image]
opt-level = 2

[profile.dev.package.livekit-cameras]
opt-level = 2

# panic = "abort" removes unwinding, so a panic in the loop ends the executor
# rather than unwinding through it; the servos keep holding their last goal.
[profile.release]
lto = true
codegen-units = 1
strip = true
panic = "abort"

[project]
name = "hebbian-rua"
description = "Build robot-use agents with your own model and loop"
readme = "README.md"
version = "0.1.2"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
license = "MIT"
license-files = [
    "LICENSE",
]
authors = [
    { name = "Hebbian Robotics" },
]
dependencies = [
    "httpx2>=2.16.0",
    "pydantic>=2.11",
    "python-dotenv>=1.2.4",
]

[project.urls]
Repository = "https://github.com/Hebbian-Robotics/rua"
Documentation = "https://github.com/Hebbian-Robotics/rua#readme"

[project.optional-dependencies]
openai = [
    "openai>=3.49.0",
]
anthropic = [
    "anthropic>=2.8.0",
]
gemini = [
    "google-genai>=3.1.0",
]

[project.scripts]
rua = "hebbian_rua.cli:main"

[build-system]
requires = [
    "uv_build>=0.13.6,<0.14",
]
build-backend = "uv_build"

[tool.uv]
exclude-newer = "3 days"

[tool.uv.build-backend]
module-root = ""
module-name = "hebbian_rua"

[tool.uv.sources.hebbian-rua]
workspace = true

[tool.uv.sources.rua-dev]
workspace = true

[tool.uv.workspace]
members = [
    "tooling",
]
exclude = [
    "examples/python",
    "examples/mujoco_sim",
]

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 88
target-version = "py312"

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E",
    "W",
    "F",
    "I",
    "B",
    "C4",
    "UP",
    "ANN",
    "PTH",
    "RET",
    "SIM",
    "TID",
    "RUF",
]
ignore = [
    "E501",
    "B008",
    "C901",
    "RET504",
    "ANN401",
]

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"
indent-style = "space"

[tool.ty.rules]
division-by-zero = "error"
deprecated = "error"
unused-ignore-comment = "error"
possibly-unresolved-reference = "error"

[tool.ty.src]
exclude = [
    "hebbian_rua/client/contract/station_api.py",
]

[tool.ty.analysis]
allowed-unresolved-imports = [
    "onnx",
    "onnxruntime",
    "torch",
]

[[tool.ty.overrides]]
include = [
    "scripts/export_so101_policy_onnx.py",
]

[tool.ty.overrides.rules]
incompatible-mutable-override = "ignore"

[tool.ty.environment]
extra-paths = []

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = [
    "tests",
]

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "rua-dev",
    "openai>=3.49.0",
    "anthropic>=2.8.0",
    "google-genai>=3.1.0",
    "datamodel-code-generator>=0.89.0",
    "jsonref>=1.1.0",
    "pytest>=9.2.0",
    "ruff",
    "ty",
]

[package]
name = "station-access"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2024"
rust-version = "1.92"
license = "MIT"
publish = false

[dependencies]
hebbian-contracts = { path = "../contracts" }
livekit-api = { version = "=0.9.1", default-features = false, features = ["access-token", "services", "rustls-tls-native-roots"] }
livekit-camera-invite = { git = "https://github.com/Hebbian-Robotics/livekit-cameras", rev = "fc1d8d67394b081ecb2244b689325b464304c0d8" }
serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1"
schemars = "1"
thiserror = "2"
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["time"] }
uuid = { version = "1", features = ["v4"] }

[lints]
workspace = true

[dev-dependencies]
base64 = "0.22"
url = "2"

[project]
name = "rua-dev"
version = "0.1.2"
description = "Development and release commands for the RUA source checkout"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
dependencies = [
    "cyclopts>=5.3.2",
    "hebbian-rua==0.1.2",
    "jsonref>=1.1.0",
    "packaging>=26.3",
    "pydantic>=2.11",
    "wheel>=0.45",
    "tomli-w>=1.2,<2",
]

[project.scripts]
rua-dev = "rua_dev.cli:main"

[build-system]
requires = ["uv_build>=0.13.6,<0.14"]
build-backend = "uv_build"

[tool.uv.build-backend]
module-root = ""
module-name = "rua_dev"

[package]
name = "hebbian-contracts"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2024"
rust-version = "1.92"
license = "MIT"
publish = false

[dependencies]
hebbian-robot-geometry = { path = "../robot-geometry", default-features = false }
serde_json = "1"
schemars = "1"
serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }

[lints]
workspace = true

[project]
name = "hebbian-robot-use-media"
description = "Camera, streaming and recording service for Hebbian Robot Use"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
authors = [{ name = "Hebbian Robotics" }]
license = "MIT"
dynamic = ["version"]

[build-system]
requires = ["maturin>=1.7,<2"]
build-backend = "maturin"

[tool.maturin]
bindings = "bin"
data = "wheel-data"

[project]
name = "hebbian-robot-use-server"
description = "The Hebbian arm executor: a prebuilt real-time control loop, installed as the `hebbian-robot-use-server` command"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
authors = [{ name = "Hebbian Robotics" }]
license = "MIT"
dynamic = ["version"]

# Maturin installs the binary on PATH. The wheel's data contains the profiles,
# robot models, viewer and notices; media is distributed separately.
[build-system]
requires = ["maturin>=1.7,<2"]
build-backend = "maturin"

[tool.maturin]
bindings = "bin"
data = "wheel-data"

[package]
name = "recordings"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2024"
license = "MIT"
publish = false
default-run = "hebbian-robot-use-recordings"

[[bin]]
name = "hebbian-robot-use-recordings"
path = "src/main.rs"

[dependencies]
axum = "0.8.9"
clap = { version = "4.6.7", features = ["derive"] }
schemars = "1"
serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1"
thiserror = "2"
tokio = { version = "1.54.1", features = ["rt-multi-thread", "macros", "net", "signal"] }
tower = { version = "0.5", features = ["util"] }
tower-http = { version = "0.6", features = ["fs", "set-header"] }

[dev-dependencies]
tempfile = "3"
http-body-util = "0.1"

[lints]
workspace = true

[project]
name = "rua-python-examples"
version = "0.1.1"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
dependencies = ["hebbian-rua==0.1.1", "openai>=3.49.0", "anthropic>=2.8.0", "google-genai>=3.1.0"]

[tool.uv]
package = false
exclude-newer = "3 days"

[tool.uv.sources]
hebbian-rua = { path = "../..", editable = true }
